# AppleSkinPumpkin

<!-- docs:begin summary -->
<!-- Generated by pumpkin-plugins-docs. Edit src/info.ts, then run `pnpm readme`. -->

AppleSkin serer-side support
<!-- docs:end summary -->

## Installation

Put `apple-skin-pumpkin.wasm` from the plugin's GitHub release in your server's `plugins/` folder and restart. Hot reload cannot ask for permissions, so the first load needs a restart.

## How it works

Vanilla tells a client about saturation only when it reaches zero, and never sends exhaustion at
all, which leaves the food tooltips AppleSkin draws behind by a tick. So the plugin reads every
online player once per tick and sends the two values, plus whether the world heals players by food.
It sends only what moved since the last packet, so a still player costs nothing.

AppleSkin is a Java Edition mod, so Bedrock players are skipped.

## Seeing what it does

Set `log.level` to `debug` in your Pumpkin config. Every packet the plugin sends is then logged with
the player and the value, along with players joining, leaving and being skipped. Ticks where nothing
changed are silent, which is the point of only sending on a change.
